failure_summary.description: Agents repeated searches or processed unchanged domains instead of updating only the affected request from compatible cached results.
Agents mishandled a return-only request or represented a round trip with arrival_date instead of separate directional legs.
Agents omitted required result saving or saved an undefined result variable.
A bare request for a specific restaurant rating was treated as a minimum rather than an exact rating.
For restaurants requested near a hotel, the agent grouped by the reference hotel rather than the requested restaurants.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers saving returned results and separate round-trip searches, so those existing instructions need no duplicate patch. These edits make the cache decision rule more operational, cover the missing return-only case, and clarify two ambiguous mappings that led to incorrect tool arguments.

edits.target: Do not repeat a base search just to add filterable criteria or regenerate unaffected domains or legs. Search only when no cached result can cover the changed scope.
edits.content: When a changed request has a compatible cached candidate set and the new requirement is filterable, retrieve the best compatible result by its exact key, apply the relevant filter, and save it; do not repeat its base search. Do not rerun or re-filter domains or legs that the latest turn did not change. If the latest turn supplies missing required information for a previously pending request, make that request actionable while leaving already satisfied domains untouched. Search only when no compatible cached result can cover the request or a new request has no cached results.

edits.target: Do not combine distinct legs by repeating keyword arguments in one call.
edits.content: If the user explicitly requests only the return flight, search only the reverse of the established route on the return date; do not search the outbound leg or encode the return date as `arrival_date` on an outbound search.

edits.target: For restaurant ratings and hotel guest ratings, interpret a requested “N-star rating” or “N or higher” as a minimum threshold unless the user explicitly requests an exact rating; use the inclusive range `[N, 5]` in `rating`. Use `[N, N]` only for an explicitly exact rating.
edits.content: For restaurant ratings and hotel guest ratings, phrases such as “at least N,” “N or higher,” or “minimum N” mean a threshold; use the inclusive range `[N, 5]` in `rating`. A bare request for “a N rating” or “rating N” means an exact rating; use `[N, N]` unless the user indicates a threshold.

edits.target: Set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants prioritized.
edits.content: Set `groupBy` to the domain being located, not the reference domain. For example, for “restaurants near the hotel,” use `groupBy="restaurant"`; for “hotels near attractions,” use `groupBy="hotel"`.
